justification: The frame is set in the opening ('the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns' / 'The explanation is as settled as the count') and then dismantled: Calverend 'thinks the count is right and the reason is wrong', Grendisham attacks his clock, Steadgrove moves the cause 'to the contract' - i.e. an accepted rule about which dryers burn plus three rival accounts of why, which is exactly D. A fails because no price series is given at all; the only money figures are 'so much per ton per point of moisture' and 'Cleaning has sold a great many service contracts', neither tracked 'across nine harvests' (the nine harvests supply the fire count, not prices). B is a real point but a subordinate one, made by a single speaker about a single objection ('On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window'); the text is not mainly a piece about investigative method. C never appears: the custom operators dry 'for their neighbors as well as themselves' and nobody argues that small farms should dry their own crop instead.

Direct span: 'His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent' - equal dirt, which is B. A inverts that same clause ('within a few percent' excludes 'several times as much'). C is refuted twice over: the swabbed machines are described as ones 'that had never burned', not as new, and both types 'carried' fines, so nothing supports 'nothing at all had gathered'; no pot of new ducts exists in the text. D is contradicted by how every party treats the result - Steadgrove 'accepts the swabs', the writer says 'The swabs are hard to walk past' and that the old advice 'rests on a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show, and nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground'; sample size is nowhere raised as an objection, whereas the clock explicitly is.

Grendisham's own words carry it: 'The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught' - noticed, not begun, which is C, reinforced by 'It looks late because nobody was there to see it early.' A is the reverse of her complaint: she says that setting the controller stop-time and the call-time 'side by side' manufactures the apparent lateness, so the two times precisely do not line up with when the fire began. B is unsupported - the sixty-one files are the fire department's log for the county, and her service department's coverage is only ever raised about swabs ('her crews still pull buckets of fines in February'), never as a limit on the log. D overshoots: she disputes what one number in the file means, not the log's evidentiary status; indeed she uses the file's numbers herself to make her case.

Steadgrove's move is 'Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing' - the operative pressure in those days is a calendar/contract pressure that reaches everyone drying grain irrespective of the machine they own, which is A ('the machine stops mattering' is the licence for 'whatever they own'). B misreads the arithmetic: forty-nine of sixty-one leaves twelve fires outside the stretch, roughly a fifth, which is not 'hardly a fire'. C is contradicted head-on by the closing paragraph: 'Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators' - the schedule is the elevators' instrument, not the mutual's. D is never asserted; the only hint of backlog is 'with trucks waiting' inside the closing rhetorical question about one operator at two in the morning, and even there the constraint described is the delivery window and the absence of a watcher, not throughput exceeding drying capacity.

The verdict sentence is explicit: 'Until then Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it' - fits the facts, untested, i.e. C, prepared by 'Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these; it needs a probe inside a machine that later burns, and nobody has one.' A is the direct negation of 'has not been answered'. B fails because the writer does adjudicate: she rules the dirt explanation dead ('nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground'), rules Grendisham's objection live, and frames what 'the mutual has to settle' - that is judgement, not abstention. D overstates: she notes his remedy 'is nearly free - run the fan on for twenty minutes after the burner cuts', but immediately withholds endorsement, 'Whether writing a run-on clause into next year's policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check.'

The gap needs the fixed collocation in 'to take the long ___', and only 'view' completes the idiom take the long view, which fits the sense demanded by the context - twelve years of patience ('which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key') accepted with good grace ('in the politest possible terms'). A 'outlook' shares the semantic field but is not the idiom: an outlook is had or held, not taken, and 'take the long outlook' is not English. B 'gaze' is literal ocular vocabulary and collocates with hold/meet, not with a metaphor about patience over years. D 'sight' would give 'take the long sight', which is likewise unidiomatic; the near-idioms with sight (lose sight of, at first sight) do not license it here.

The sentence adverbial must set up the concession that the following lines spell out: the no-inheritance rule holds as written but not in practice - 'That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd. It is simply not what the list runs on.' 'Strictly' is the standard marker of that strictly-speaking/in-practice contrast. C 'Curiously' is excluded by the very next lines, which deny any oddity: 'nobody disputes it or finds it odd'. A 'Increasingly' requires a change over time in the rule, but the clause is presented as constant and categorical ('The tenancy ends when the tenant does'); nothing in the paragraph is diachronic. D 'Privately' would mark a contrast between public and private positions, but the rule is the association's written, public clause, and the passage stresses that nothing is concealed ('Nothing here is hidden: the order is numbered').

The gap completes the set idiom in 'waiting for dead men's ___', which in English is dead men's shoes - and the paragraph supplies exactly its meaning, that advancement comes only when a predecessor drops out: 'Movement comes when somebody else stops - a knee that will not manage the walk from the gate ... a winter that settles it', with the follow-up 'It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke' marking it as a known grim phrase rather than an invention. B 'coats', C 'gloves' and D 'hats' are all plausible articles of clothing but none of them is an English idiom in this frame; substituting any of them destroys the recognisability the sentence relies on when it calls the wording 'a phrase for this among themselves'.

The frame 'the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either' requires the opposite pole of approving, so that the sentence brackets the tone as neutral between praise and blame; 'censorious' (fault-finding, condemnatory) is that pole, and it suits the studied blankness of 'the minutes give it one line'. A 'gracious' sits on the same positive side as 'approving', so 'not approving, but not gracious either' is a redundancy rather than the intended contrast - the sentence would say nothing. B 'cautious' and C 'anxious' name the writer's confidence or mood, not the approve/disapprove axis the first half establishes; a minute can be both cautious and approving, so neither yields the required 'either' opposition.

The object is a rule, and the verb needed is the one that means put into effect / appeal to as authority: 'The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been invoked' - the point being that after 'Three times the answer was no', the committee has quietly declined to apply it, which is why 'One name has stood at the top since 2019.' D 'evoked' is the classic near-homograph trap: it means to call up a memory, image or feeling, and rules are not evoked. B 'provoked' takes reactions or people as objects (provoked a response), and would absurdly make the rule the thing produced rather than the thing applied. A 'summoned' takes persons, courage or help, not a written rule, and would misdescribe an administrative act as a calling-in of someone.

The passage's whole payload is in 'Height is the part worth reading. The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack, the flue from the attic bedroom, with the least warm air beneath it to do the lifting' - a raised pot is a repair for poor draught, which is A ('drawing badly' = 'smoked', with the cause given as too little warm air to lift the gases). B misassigns the purpose of the narrowing: 'Narrowing the mouth helps as well, since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening' - it is stated as a second draught remedy, and rain or birds are never mentioned. C is the reverse of the text's opening judgement, 'the pots seldom match. Pattern tells you very little', with the reason given that 'Builders' yards sold whatever was in stock' and that a 1961 rebuild 'carries what came off the lorry'; ornament is explicitly attributed to householders wanting 'to tell their own door from thirty identical ones', not to flue trouble. D contradicts the same lines - stock and chance, not matching to ridge tiles or brickwork, determined what was fitted.

The numbers are constructed to be read against the clock: the chandler's hatch 'opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390', and 'Both shut when the evening cart went at eight' - about thirteen hours against six, yet a difference of only twenty-two letters, which implies the volume was set by the deadline everyone posted against rather than by how long the flap was open, i.e. D. B states the naive opposite of that arithmetic: 412 against 390 is not 'far more'. C is contradicted by the same sentence that both 'shut when the evening cart went at eight' - the bookseller stayed open no later than the chandler and so made up nothing after the cart. A is the tempting incentive story (the keeper 'was allowed threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves'), but the passage gives no evidence that hours were stretched for the allowance, and its one comparable data point cuts against a claim about both houses: the bookseller 'opened at two', forgoing seven billable hours, which is the last thing an allowance-maximiser would do. The surveyor noticing only that 'the chandler's flap wanted a new spring' likewise records no complaint of padded hours.

Foljden ges rakt ut: 'Arbetet gjordes sent pa hosten, nar vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen gravdes upp i smala rutor, lades i hogar pa fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern over, tills frosten hade sprangt sonder klumparna ... Forst darefter rostades den pa en badd av ved' - senhost, uteliggande vinter, rostning sist, vilket ar C. A bryter mot bada leden: upptagningen skedde inte 'pa varvintern, medan tjalen bar' utan sent pa hosten, och rostningen kom efter, inte fore, hogen ('Forst darefter rostades den'). B motsags av 'Langt ifran varje mosse bar ett sadant skikt, och de som gor det bar det ojamnt'. D motsags av 'Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, for pa ytan syns det inte'; blot mark namns bara som skalet att vanta till hosten, 'nar vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan', alltsa tvartom torrare forhallanden.

Tolvsaters forsta resultat: 'De blasningar som drevs hardast, med tatare balgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte storre luppar utan sprodare: kolet gick in i jarnet, och klumpen sprack under slaggan i stallet for att lata sig strackas' - hardare drift, hogre kolhalt, sprodare jarn, vilket ar A. B kastar om riktningen: sprodheten hor till de hardast drivna, inte de svagast drivna blasningarna. C overdriver till kategoriskt misslyckande; texten sager att lupparna blev sprodare, inte att 'samtliga blasningar misslyckades', och de trettiosex blasningarna redovisas som tva tydliga resultat, inte som ett haveri. D pekar pa fel foremal: torkningen av lergodset diskuteras i ugnsavsnittet ('Innan den kunde fyllas maste den torkas langsamt'), alltsa som bakgrund om byggnaden, medan forsokens tva redovisade utfall galler kolupptag och slaggens jarnhalt.

Texten gor sjalv kopplingen: 'Det ar hantverkets utgangspunkt. Jarnet reducerades i fast form ... det som blev kvar bakades ihop till en klump som aldrig runnit nagonstans', och darpa 'Ur detta foljer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blasning gav nagra kilo jarn ... Tyngdpunkten i arbetet lag inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efterat, i rackningen' - fast fas forklarar bade luppens ringa storlek och arbetets tyngdpunkt, vilket ar D. A motsags av dateringen 'Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet'; nagot bygdejarn langt in pa 1800-talet finns inte. B kastar om ordningen: det var hyttan, den senare tekniken, som 'kravde vattenkraft och standig drift', medan blastugnen 'kostade lera, sten och ved'. C motsags av 'uppteckningarna, som ar utforliga om vem som agde vad, sager nastan ingenting om sjalva blasningen'.

Forsokens andra resultat ger slutsatsen: 'den jarnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lagre jarnhalt blir trogflytande vid de temperaturer en sadan ugn orkar halla; den rinner inte undan utan blir kvar kring kornen, och luppen gar da inte att rensa. Jarnet i avfallet ar priset for att slaggen alls ska lamna schaktet' - alltsa B. A ar just Krokvalls tolkning, 'ett tecken pa dalig kontroll', och texten avvisar den uttryckligen: 'det ar tolkningen av dem som forsoken talar emot'. C motsags av 'Krokvalls matvarden har ingen ifragasatt'; Tolvsater har blast ugnar, inte lagt fram konkurrerande matserier. D bygger in en forklaring texten forvagrar: om spridningen mellan ugnsplatser heter det att 'varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas matt racker for att forklara spridningen', sa jarnforlusten kan inte aberopas som dess forklaring - och varpens storlek diskuteras bara som det som gor platserna mojliga att hitta.

Skribenten sager bade att behovet finns och att finansieringsvagen ar fel: 'Att atgarder behovs ar ingen stridsfraga' med den kapade linan och stegen som 'slutar en halvmeter ovanfor vattenytan', och sedan 'Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min rost', med den positiva slutsatsen 'Kop bojarna, badstegen och hjartstartaren over driftsbudgeten' - utrustning ja, avgift nej, vilket ar D. A finns inte i texten; hon foreslar aldrig en hogre taxa utan en annan finansieringskalla, och hennes invandningar galler betalningsgrad och omfordelat badande, inte nivan. B motsags av skadebilden - kapad lina, for hog badstege, narmaste hjartstartare '2,3 kilometer bort' - som just visar att befintlig utrustning inte racker. C motsags av aterkallandet av rosten och av risken hon anfor, att 'en avgift vid bryggan lar forskjuta en del av badandet just dit' dar ingen utrustning finns.

Sifferspannet ar entydigt: 'Kommunens egen uppfoljning landade pa en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gastnatterna', alltsa knappt sju av tio natter obetalda, vilket ar A. C ar spegelvandningen av samma tal och stupar pa 31 procent. B motsags av att matningen faktiskt genomfordes och redovisades som en siffra ('Kommunens egen uppfoljning landade pa'); det texten kallar svagt ar drivkrafterna att betala vid bryggan, dar det 'finns varken bom, vakt eller registreringsskylt att fotografera av', inte matbarheten. D saknar stod: skylten beskrivs som kvarvarande del av ordningen vid stallplatsen ('en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gasten skannar') och ingenting sags om att den togs ned.

Genomgangen av de drygt trehundra anmalningarna ger: 'I de fall dar skriften gick att jamfora med annat i mappen harrorde yrkesordet i regel fran abonnenten sjalv' - precis D, med reservationen 'dar skriften gick att jamfora' bevarad. A ar den motsatta slutsatsen och tillhor en av de mekanismer hon sokte men inte fann ('en kassor med bestamda uppfattningar om vem som var kopman'), avfardad med 'Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltsa'. B overtolkar overstrykningarna; texten sager uttryckligen att de 'kan lika garna vara andrade beslut som rattelser av en fellasning - materialet svarar inte pa det'. C motsags direkt av 'Titelraden var tom pa den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista over godkanda ord, ingen anvisning om langd'.

Hon ger upp misstanken sjalv: 'Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltsa. Jag far ge Ramnestad ratt, och den forklaring som fran borjan lag narmast ar ocksa den som star kvar' - det vill saga fafangan, 'Folk satte ett finare ord pa sig sjalva nar tillfallet gavs', vilket ar B, forstarkt av det tidigare 'Dar hade jag fel'. A ar raka motsatsen till 'Jag far ge Ramnestad ratt'. C forvaxlar de kvarstaende smadetaljerna med huvudfragan: 'Ett par saker far jag anda inte att ga ihop' galler de fyra hemmansagarnas tomma rad, ankornas titlar och overstrykningarna, medan huvudfragan om vem som valde orden ar avgjord. D finns inte; foreningsstyrning avvisas helt, sa nagon kombination av forklaringar foreslas aldrig.

The text opens on a settled local rule -- "the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns" -- and then spends four paragraphs on rival accounts of WHY (Calverend's shutdown timing, Grendisham's unmanned-site objection, Steadgrove's contract/deduction-schedule move), closing with "nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground" and "Grendisham's objection has not been answered": a familiar rule plus a disputed cause, so D. A fails because price appears only as an incidental clause -- "at so much per ton per point of moisture" -- with no movement across nine harvests ever traced. B mistakes one participant's rebuttal for the topic: the unmanned-site problem is Grendisham's single objection ("that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught"), one strand of the dispute, not its subject. C is absent from the text entirely; custom operations "drying for their neighbors as well as themselves" are described as a fire-log demographic, never as a choice small farms are urged to reconsider.

"His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent" -- equal dirt loading, so B. A inverts the finding: "within a few percent" excludes "several times as much," and the whole point of the swabs is that they undercut the dirt explanation ("The county's standard advice rests on a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show"). C overshoots to zero: the ducts "collect fines" on both machine types and Grendisham's crews "still pull buckets of fines," so the swabs found comparable dirt, not none. D imports a sample-size complaint no one makes; the narrator's verdict is the opposite -- "The swabs are hard to walk past" -- and even Steadgrove "accepts the swabs."

Grendisham's argument is that the log's second timestamp is a discovery time: "The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught" -- hence "It looks late because nobody was there to see it early": noticed, not begun, so C. A reverses her: she says the two numbers only LOOK aligned into lateness -- "Set those two numbers side by side and of course the fire looks late" -- i.e. the call time and the controller stop time do not measure the same event. B is a coverage claim never made; the log is the fire department's record of sixty-one fires county-wide, and her service department's reach is raised only about swabs ("her crews still pull buckets of fines in February"). D misstates her: she treats the log as usable evidence and disputes its interpretation, calling the clock "the weak joint in the argument," not the record illegitimate.

Steadgrove's reframing is that the date, not the hardware, explains the cluster: "Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, he argues, and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing" -- a schedule and a delivery window imposed by the elevators on everyone hauling grain, which is why he moves the cause "to the contract." That is A: the same commercial squeeze regardless of which machine you own. B overstates the arithmetic -- forty-nine of sixty-one leaves twelve fires outside the stretch, roughly a fifth, which "hardly a fire" cannot describe. C is contradicted directly: "Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators" -- the schedule is not the mutual's to rewrite. D asserts a capacity shortfall the text never claims; "with trucks waiting" appears only inside the closing rhetorical scene about one operator at two in the morning, and no comparison of arrival rate to drying throughput is anywhere made.

The closing assessment is explicit: "Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these; it needs a probe inside a machine that later burns, and nobody has one. Until then Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it" -- fits but untested, so C. A is the flat negation of "has not been answered." B fails because the writer does adjudicate rather than abstain: she rules on the swabs ("The swabs are hard to walk past"; "nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground") and on the clock's untestedness, taking positions on both. D reads her past her own hedge: on the run-on clause she writes "Whether writing a run-on clause into next year's policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check," and ends on an open question -- she notes the remedy is "nearly free," not that she endorses adopting it.

The gap completes the fixed idiom "take the long view," and the context builds it exactly: the bottom of the list is "twelve years from a key," and the newcomer is "being asked, in the politest possible terms" to accept that horizon -- to take the long view. A fails as collocation: "outlook" takes have/adopt (a long-term outlook), never "take the long outlook." B is wrong in sense as well as collocation -- a "gaze" is a physical act of looking, and "take the long gaze" is not English. D likewise: "long sight" names an eye condition (long-sightedness) and "take the long sight" is not an idiom; only "view" carries the required sense of a patient, extended perspective on time.

The sentence introduces the written rule that practice then departs from: "a plot cannot be inherited. The tenancy ends when the tenant does... That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd. It is simply not what the list runs on." "Strictly" is the standard hedge for stating a rule as literally written against how things actually work, so B. C is killed by the very next clause -- "nobody disputes it or finds it odd" cancels "Curiously" outright. A requires a trend over time that the paragraph never supplies; the clause is a fixed rule, not something increasingly true. D contradicts the paragraph's own framing: the clause is public and formal ("That is the clause as written"), the opposite of a private arrangement, and it is the informal succession later in the text -- the nephew, the minutes -- that is the unofficial part.

The gap completes the set idiom "waiting for dead men's shoes," meaning advancement that depends on someone's death -- precisely the paragraph's content: "Movement comes when somebody else stops -- a knee that will not manage the walk from the gate... a winter that settles it," and "It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke." B, C and D all fail as idiom rather than as sense: "dead men's coats," "dead men's gloves" and "dead men's hats" are not English phrases and carry none of the succession meaning, whereas stepping into a dead man's shoes is the fixed image for taking over a vacated place, which is exactly what the numbered waiting list delivers.

The frame is a concessive pair -- "the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either" -- which needs a term at the opposite pole from approving, i.e. openly condemnatory. "Censorious" (severely critical, faultfinding) is that word, so D, and it matches the minutes' one flat line about the nephew's tenancy: neither blessing nor rebuke. A collapses the contrast: "gracious" sits on the same warm side as "approving," so "not approving, but not gracious either" states no opposition at all. B and C name the writer's or the committee's emotional state rather than the tone of a judgement -- a minuted line can be cautious or anxious without that being the counter-pole of approval, and neither yields the required not-praise/not-blame axis that the sentence's "but... either" construction demands.

The object is a rule: "The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___" -- and the verb that takes a rule as object, meaning formally applied or appealed to, is "invoked," so C; it reports that despite three refusals by the name that has "stood at the top since 2019," nobody has enforced the clause. A miscollocates: one summons a person, a meeting or a witness, not a rule. B reverses the direction of agency -- a rule provokes a reaction rather than being provoked, and "provoke" requires an emotion or response as object. D is the classic near-miss: "evoke" means to call up a memory, image or feeling, so it takes atmospheres and associations, not regulations; only "invoke" carries the sense of putting a rule into operation.

The height paragraph is explicit: "Height is the part worth reading. The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack, the flue from the attic bedroom, with the least warm air beneath it to do the lifting" -- a smoking flue is one drawing badly, and the taller pot is the retrofit cure, so A. B assigns the wrong purpose: the text gives a draught reason, not a weather one -- "Narrowing the mouth helps as well, since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening" -- and rain and birds are never mentioned. C is refuted by "Pattern tells you very little," the sentence that explicitly separates ornament from diagnosis and hands that job to height. D is contradicted twice over: "the pots seldom match," and their selection is traced to stock and vanity -- "Builders' yards sold whatever was in stock, householders bought ornament to tell their own door from thirty identical ones" -- not to matching ridge tiles or brickwork.

The numbers are the argument: the chandler's hatch "opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390," and "Both shut when the evening cart went at eight." Thirteen hours against six yields only twenty-two extra letters, so the extra morning produced almost nothing and the traffic must be massing against the cart's eight o'clock departure -- the deadline, not the duration, sets the count, hence D. B misreads that same pair: 412 against 390 is under six percent, which "far more" cannot describe, and the whole point of the pairing is how little the long day bought. C is contradicted by "Both shut when the evening cart went at eight" -- the bookseller stayed open no later than his rival, so he made up his late start within the same closing hour, not after it. A attributes a motive the text does not support and that the bookseller falsifies: the pay rule is stated ("threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves") but one of the two keepers opened only at two, so the keepers as a pair were not stretching hours for the allowance, and the surveyor's note records nothing but "the chandler's flap wanted a new spring."

Sekvensen är utskriven i första stycket: ”Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över, tills frosten hade sprängt sönder klumparna och regnet sköljt bort mullen. Först därefter rostades den” – senhöst, uteliggande vinter, därefter rostning, alltså C. A vänder både tid och ordning: uppgrävningen sker sent på hösten och inte på vårvintern, och rostningen kommer uttryckligen efter högen (”Först därefter rostades den”), inte före. B motsägs direkt av ”Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt, och de som gör det bär det ojämnt”. D motsägs av ”Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte” – markens blöta är inget undantag från spettet, och det var tvärtom när vattnet sjunkit undan som arbetet gjordes.

Det första av Tolvsäters två tydliga resultat lyder: ”De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan i stället för att låta sig sträckas” – hårdare drift, högre kolhalt, sprödare järn, alltså A. B är den exakta inversionen: sprödheten följde av hårdare, inte svagare, drift. C överdriver till totalt misslyckande – texten säger att hårdare drivna blåsningar gav sprödare luppar, inte att samtliga blåsningar havererade så snart bälgtagen tätnade, och trettiosex blåsningar gav tvärtom två användbara resultat. D flyttar över fyndet till fel stycke: torkning och murning behandlas i beskrivningen av ugnen (”Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt”), medan försökens två redovisade resultat gäller kolhalt/sprödhet och slaggens järnhalt som villkor.

Texten gör den fasta reduktionen till förklaringsgrund: ”Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt. Järnet reducerades i fast form... Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn... Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen” – alltså både luppens ringa storlek och arbetets tyngdpunkt, vilket är D. A spränger dateringen: ”Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet”, och övergången till bruken beskrivs som redan fullbordad med hyttan. B kastar om kronologin: det var hyttan, ”som kom senare”, som ”krävde vattenkraft och ständig drift”, medan blästugnen bara kostade ”lera, sten och ved”. C motsägs av slutsatsen om källorna: ”uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen”.

Försöken vänder om tolkningen av Krokvalls värden: ”den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla; den rinner inte undan utan blir kvar kring kornen, och luppen går då inte att rensa. Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet” – alltså B. A är Krokvalls förkastade läsning (”Krokvall läste det som ett tecken på dålig kontroll”), som försöken uttryckligen talar emot. C är fel om vad som är omtvistat: ”Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt; det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot”, och Tolvsäter presenteras inte som en konkurrerande mätning. D ger slaggen en förklaringskraft som texten uttryckligen fråntar den: om spridningen mellan platser heter det att ”varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen”, och utbytesskillnaden står kvar som oförklarad under ”Mycket är ändå oklart”.

Skribenten återkallar sin röst men inte behovet: ”Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst” ställs mot ”Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”, och slutklämmen ger alternativet – ”Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten, och sätt upp en kastlina vid Stångklippan också”. Utrustning ja, avgift som finansieringsväg nej, alltså D. A missar att invändningen är principiell och inte en nivåfråga: kritiken gäller betalningsgraden (31 procent vid ställplatsen) och omfördelningen till Stångklippan, aldrig att tjugo kronor vore för lite. B motsägs av tillståndsbeskrivningen – ”en livboj vars lina någon har kapat”, ”badstegen slutar en halvmeter ovanför vattenytan”, närmaste hjärtstartare 2,3 kilometer bort – utrustningen finns alltså inte att sköta. C är den röst hon uttryckligen tar tillbaka, och hennes tyngsta invändning är just att avgiften ”lär förskjuta en del av badandet” till den plats där elva av fjorton tillbud inträffat.

Ställplatsen anförs som prejudikat för tillitsbetalning: ”Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna” – alltså förblev ungefär sju nätter av tio obetalda, vilket är A. B motsägs av att siffran finns och är kommunens egen uppföljning; det som beskrivs som svagare vid bryggan är drivkrafterna, där det ”varken [finns] bom, vakt eller registreringsskylt att fotografera av”, inte mätbarheten. C vänder på procenttalet: 31 procent betalda är det motsatta av ”nästan alla”. D lägger till en händelse texten inte har – skylten beskrivs som alltjämt del av ordningen (”en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar”), och inget sägs om att den togs ned.

Genomgången av anmälningarna ger flera fynd, och det som svarar på frågan är: ”I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv” – med reservationen inbyggd, alltså D. A är den hypotes fyndet slår undan (”en kassör med bestämda uppfattningar om vem som var köpman”), och slutsatsen lyder ”Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså”. B påstår en tolkning som texten uttryckligen lämnar oavgjord: ”överstrykningarna kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning – materialet svarar inte på det”. C motsägs ordagrant av ”Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd”.

Skribenten kapitulerar uttryckligen: ”Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar” – det vill säga fåfängan, ”Folk satte ett finare ord på sig själva när tillfället gavs”, alltså B. A är raka motsatsen till ”Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt”; hon medger till och med sin felbedömning av arkivarien: ”jag tog det för ett tecken på att han aldrig hade prövat saken. Där hade jag fel”. C förväxlar en avgjord huvudfråga med kvarstående detaljer – ”Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop” gäller hemmansägarnas tomma rader, änkornas titlar och överstrykningarna, inte om föreningen styrde orden. D bygger på en sammanjämkning texten inte gör: hennes egna mekanismer förkastas i sin helhet, så någon kombination av förklaringar erbjuds aldrig.
